# h5i-db

> h5i-db is a high-performance, embedded, versioned analytical database for quantitative finance and time-series workloads. It runs full DataFusion SQL with native ASOF joins, OHLCV/VWAP rollups, time travel, and previewable mutations over immutable, time-sorted Parquet segments — driven from a CLI, Rust, or Python, and designed to be safe for AI agents. Written in Rust; Apache-2.0.

A database is a single directory on disk; there is no server. Every write is an atomic commit that produces a new immutable version, and any past version is readable in O(1). Storage is time-sorted and pruned by manifest statistics before I/O. Destructive changes (delete/replace ranges) can be staged as previewable plans and gated by a mutation policy. The CLI emits machine-readable output and structured errors with stable exit codes.

## Manual
- [Overview](https://db.h5i.dev/manual/index.html): What h5i-db is, what it is for, and how the documentation is organized.
- [Installation](https://db.h5i.dev/manual/installation.html): Install the h5i-db CLI and Python library, or build both from source.
- [Quickstart](https://db.h5i.dev/manual/quickstart.html): From nothing to a queried, versioned market database in five commands — CLI and Python.
- [Migrating from DuckDB](https://db.h5i.dev/manual/migrating-from-duckdb.html): Move tables from a .duckdb file into a versioned h5i-db store using DuckDB's own Parquet export, plus a SQL dialect and workflow checklist for what changes.
- [Core concepts](https://db.h5i.dev/manual/concepts.html): Versions, segments, manifests, snapshots, previewable mutation plans, and the mutation policy — the mental model behind h5i-db.
- [CLI reference](https://db.h5i.dev/manual/cli.html): Every command, flag, output format, and exit code of the h5i-db command-line tool.
- [SQL reference](https://db.h5i.dev/manual/sql.html): h5i-db's SQL surface beyond stock DataFusion: time travel with h5i(), ASOF joins, gapfill/resample, tail, time_bucket, vwap, ewma, and rolling window sugar.
- [Agents & automation](https://db.h5i.dev/manual/agents.html): The machine contract: structured output and errors, stable exit codes, resource limits as flags, and policy-gated review for AI agents and pipelines.
- [Operations guide](https://db.h5i.dev/manual/operations.html): Running h5i-db in production: backup and restore, vacuum and compaction cadence, plan hygiene, disk-usage math, filesystem caveats, and the torn-HEAD recovery runbook.

## Python API
- [Overview](https://db.h5i.dev/api/index.html): The h5i_db Python library — install, the five-minute tour, data interchange, and error handling.
- [Database](https://db.h5i.dev/api/database.html): h5i_db.Database reference: lifecycle, tables, writing, reading and SQL, time travel, mutation plans, policy, and maintenance.
- [DataFrame builder](https://db.h5i.dev/api/dataframe.html): Build queries as Python instead of SQL strings: db.table(), lazy verbs, expressions, rolling and cross-sectional operators, ASOF joins, and the SQL each one compiles to.
- [QueryResult & MutationPlan](https://db.h5i.dev/api/results-and-plans.html): Converting query results to Arrow, pandas, and Polars; previewing and applying mutation plans.
- [Exceptions](https://db.h5i.dev/api/exceptions.html): The typed error hierarchy: every h5i-db error carries a stable code, an actionable hint, and a retryable flag.
